Hypercasual Teardown

Spinner Merge

A merge board that is also a team sheet. The player buys cheap spinners at a price that climbs ×1.5 with every tap, fuses identical pairs into fewer, stronger tops on a 5×3 grid, then presses FIGHT and watches physics decide. Each fight pays out and resets the price, so the defining decision is simple and constant: spend one more time, or fight now with the board you have.

  • Sunday.gg · iOS & Android
  • Free · ads + in-app purchases
  • Portrait, one-thumb
  • Fights of roughly 5–10 s
  • Boss every 6th level
  • Now listed as Spinner Merge Blitz

01

One board, two buttons, a 20-second loop

Almost every minute of play repeats five beats. The variety comes from which spinners sit on the board and which enemies wait above it, not from new verbs.

BuyTap SPINNER: a base-tier spinner drops into the next free cell. The next one costs about 1.5× more.
MergeDrag a spinner onto an identical one: both vanish and one spinner of the next tier appears in the target cell.
ReadThe enemy lineup already stands in the upper half of the same tray; the player can rearrange before committing.
FightTap FIGHT: every spinner launches at once and the arena resolves itself in seconds. Freeze is the only in-fight tap.
CollectCoins earned by hits, gears from kills, gems on wins. The board returns, the price resets, the next level loads.

A characteristic episode: level 2

The second level shows the full loop in under fifteen seconds. The player starts with the spinner that won level 1, still sitting in the top row of the grid. The buy button reads 15K; four taps later the price has climbed 15K → 22K → 33K → 49K, the coins are gone and the button has become a green FREE ad offer. Two pairs of the new orange spinners are dragged together into purple level-2 spinners, two purples become the first cyan level-3, and the game interrupts with an unlock card before the fight.

Nothing in that sequence asks the player to read. Price, owner and result are always on the board itself: the price on the button, the merge target lit in green, the new tier announced full-screen.

02

The board is the whole strategy

Fifteen cells, a price that compounds and a stat table that punishes over-merging slightly: three small rules that make the preparation phase a real decision.

The grid is five columns by three rows in both recorded builds. It is the only inventory: a spinner that is not on the board does not exist, and a full board blocks buying. Merging is therefore two things at once, a power upgrade and the only way to make room.

The buy button compounds

One level 7 preparation, each step ≈ ×1.5. Eight steps take the price from 90K to 2.30M; the next preparation starts again near the bottom.

Each tier grows Heart by about ×1.5

Heart (HP) per tier as printed in the game; Sword (attack) is always one quarter of Heart. Two spinners always hold more summed stats than the one they become.

L112 / 3
L220 / 5
L328 / 7
L444 / 11
L564 / 16
L692 / 23
L7140 / 35
L8208 / 52
L9308 / 77
L10464 / 116

Two level-8 spinners carry 416 Heart between them; the level 9 they merge into has 308. Every merge costs roughly a quarter (17–30%) of the summed stats in exchange for a free cell, a bigger body and, the first time, a new tier. That small tax is what keeps "merge everything" from being automatic.

Why the reset matters

Because each purchase costs about half again the last one, a single preparation quickly prices itself out: in the level 7 sequence above, the ninth spinner costs about 25 times the first. Every fight, won or lost, pays coins and the next preparation opens at a low price again (120K after a level 8 defeat, then 150K, 165K, 180K, 195K and 210K across levels 11–14). The economic rhythm is therefore "buy a few cheap ones, merge, fight, repeat", not "save up".

Higher tiers come from three sources: merging, the gem shop and the spawn level, which lifts the tier that the buy button produces (section 04). The collection screen numbers fifty tiers; the recordings reach level 10.

03

Fights are watched, not steered

Pressing FIGHT hands control to physics. The spinners bounce inside the tray's raised rim, HP bars drain on contact and every contact pays coins.

All of the player's spinners launch together from their cells toward the enemy group. There is no aiming; the only influence is the arrangement chosen before the fight and, from level 7, one tap on Freeze. Fights in the recordings last roughly five to ten seconds.

Feedback is dense and readable without sound. Each contact throws a coin popup whose value tracks the tier of the spinner that landed it: 30K for the starting purple spinner, 150K for the gold level 6, 162K, 175K and 188K for the next three tiers (the 2022 build shows the same values, with 15K, 50K, 100K and 125K for tiers 1, 3, 4 and 5). A destroyed spinner bursts into white smoke and confetti and drops blue gear tokens that fly to a counter at the top of the screen.

That makes the fight an earning phase as much as a test. Victory banks the hit coins (level 1: three 30K hits, a 90K reward), the gears from kills and a few gems; defeat banks coins and gears but no gems.

04

Three currencies on three clocks

Coins live inside one preparation, gears build a permanent upgrade over several levels, and gems buy a shortcut every few wins.

CurrencyEarned fromSpent onChanges which decision
CoinsEvery hit in a fight; win or loss; mission rewardsThe buy button (×1.5 per purchase within a preparation)How many base spinners to add before this fight
GearsDestroyed enemies (win or loss)Pouring into the casing on the build screenWhen the buy button starts producing a higher tier
GemsVictories only: 2–4 per normal win, 20–30 for a bossSpinner Shop: a chosen tier placed directly on the boardWhether to skip several merges for one strong spinner

Gears: the spawn-level casing

After a result screen the game opens a dark, unfinished spinner casing with a remaining-gears counter (84 on the first visit) and a TAP TO BUILD button. Gears pour in and the casing colours up; when the counter reaches zero a banner announces "You can now spawn level 2 spinners!" with that tier's stats. From then on the buy button produces the higher tier. The recording reaches spawn levels 2, 3 and 4 at about 1:36, 4:58 and 7:30 of play; the remaining counters grow (224 and 896 were seen when later builds started), so each step takes more fights.

This is the game's permanent progression. It also quietly changes the board decision: once the buy button gives level 3, every early merge step is skipped.

Gems: a priced shortcut

The Spinner Shop lists consecutive tiers at 10 gems per tier level (level 2 for 20, up to level 8 for 80) and the visible window moves up as the player progresses. In the recording one tap on the level 6 card spent 60 of 96 gems with no confirmation step, and a level 6 appeared on the board.

05

Every sixth level is a boss, and the first boss pays an ability

A six-node progress bar with a skull at the end frames each run of levels as a chapter, and the result screens count down to it.

Victory banners announce "Boss fight in 3 lvls!", then 2, then "Boss fight coming up!". The boss level opens with a red skull card and a promise of bonus rewards (coins ×3, gems ×5). The first boss, at level 6, is one large humanoid that stands in the arena with a long HP bar while the spinners grind against it; the level 12 boss is a pair of humanoids with separate bars.

Beating the level 6 boss unlocks Freeze ("Freeze all enemy spinners"). At the next fight a pointing hand and a speech bubble ask the player to tap it, and the frozen enemies keep taking hits under a snowflake marker. Two more ability slots stay locked with plain targets: Reach Lvl 19 and Reach Lvl 31.

The bosses in this build are recognisable third-party characters (a blue Rainbow Friends-style monster, a Slenderman-style figure and a Freddy Fazbear-style bear). They work as thumbnail bait; they are not part of what a rebuild may copy.

06

An instant first fight, and defeats that cost almost nothing

The game starts mid-action and treats losing as a paid timeout: the lineup comes back, the price resets, and the result screen still pays.

The first minute

The 2025 recording opens on level 1 with one spinner already on the board facing one enemy; the first tap is FIGHT, and three hits later the first victory pays 2 gems, 15 gears and 90K. Buying, merging, the build screen and the daily-bonus calendar all arrive within the first minute, each as a full-screen interruption; the missions list sits one tap away. The 2022 build taught the board with a pointing hand dragging a spinner into a cell; whether the current build shows a hand for the first merge is not visible in the recording.

The failure loop

At level 8 the player's five spinners lose to a lineup that includes two level 7 shurikens. The DEFEAT! screen pays 110 gears and 2.00M coins (no gems) with the same ad multiplier. Back on the board, the lineup is there again and the buy button has dropped to 120K: the player re-buys, merges up to the first level 8 and wins the retry. The same pattern repeats at levels 13 and 14. The cost of losing is time and the lost gem reward, never the board.

Two details matter for a rebuild. The retry's enemy lineup was not identical to the first attempt, and in this level 8 retry the smallest spinner (a level 2) did not return while the four bigger ones did; elsewhere the full lineup returns. Neither is explained on screen.

07

A three-year-old live game, rebuilt more than once

Spinner Merge is a Sunday.gg hypercasual title first released in October 2022 and still updated, now under the name Spinner Merge Blitz.

What a player is offered

The store copy sells exactly the loop above: "merge matching spinners", "build your team", "battle in the arena" and a line that strategy matters as well as strength. The game is free, carries ads at every result screen (multiplier wheel), on the buy button when coins run out and on mission skips, and sells in-app purchases on iOS (VIP Spinner Club $9.99, Remove Ads $5.99, three bundles at $24.99, US store, looked up 1 October 2026). Google Play tags it Merge, Casual, Single player, Stylized and Offline.

Reception

Critics—No Metacritic or OpenCritic page and no outlet review foundTypical for a hypercasual mobile release

Players rate it well on iOS and middling on Android. Written reviews point at the same things the recordings show: one widely upvoted 2022 review calls it endless and offline-friendly and says the spinner ladder tops out after many levels; a 2026 review describes a late game where the board is full of level 50 spinners and nothing more can be bought, and asks for a way to delete spinners; another complains that paying to remove ads did not remove them. These are individual opinions, not a measured consensus, and review counts say nothing reliable about sales.

The two recordings show the production principle: the merge board and the physics fight stayed fixed while every layer around them (stats, permanent spawn upgrades, a second premium currency, bosses with abilities, retention calendars) was added later. Sunday also lists a separate sibling app, Spinner Merge Masters, with very few ratings.

Side systems around the core

Missions offer three short coin tasks at a time (kill 3 spinners, complete 2 levels, watch 2 ads, later "kill 1 boss", "win 3 levels in a row", "earn 6M cash"), each skippable with an ad. A seven-day calendar pays coins and ends in a "Legendary Spinner". Neither changes the board decision; both exist to bring the player back and to place ads.

08

What to keep

One scarce surfaceA 15-cell board is inventory, team and economy at once; merging is both power and room.
A price that argues back×1.5 per buy and a reset every fight turn "buy or fight" into a fresh, cheap decision each level.
Failure that paysLosses keep the lineup and still pay coins and gears; only gems and time are lost.
Chapters of sixA visible countdown to a boss, and a boss that grants a new verb, give the endless ladder shape.

Build layer

Mobile web adaptation: Spinner Merge

Everything a builder needs is in this file: the short prompt, the rules with their evidence status, the complete target game, the design space, the Roblox hooks and the embedded evidence. Source evidence: two public YouTube recordings — V2 apYBMGRpAFU ("MAX LEVEL BLADES! - Spinner Merge", uploaded 15 May 2025, 704 s, levels 1–14; the main source) and V1 hJeqPfDfEdQ ("EVOLVING a Spinner to MAX POWER BEYBLADE - Spinner Merge", uploaded 1 Nov 2022, 688 s, levels 1–21 with jump cuts; earlier build) — analysed from an extension packet (run archived run) plus independently decoded frames. Times below are seconds of the recording.

Reading procedure for the receiving builder

  1. Parse this HTML structurally (an HTML parser, not line deletion). Read every section, including collapsed <details>; do not load base64 payloads into your text context.
  2. Extract each embedded image from its <figure id="fig-…"> into your working directory and open it with an image tool. Check that every ID in the evidence index exists.
  3. For each rule marked Verified, compare the stated values with the linked figures before relying on them. Items marked Designed are yours to design; items marked Unknown are design space.
  4. Then follow the Build prompt.

Build prompt

Build the complete mobile web game "Spinner Merge" adaptation described in this teardown, delivered as ONE self-contained HTML file that opens by double-click (all code, art, fonts and sounds inlined; no network, no server).

Fantasy: you own a tray of battle spinning tops. Buy cheap tops, fuse identical pairs into bigger and stronger ones on a 5×3 board, then press FIGHT and watch them smash an enemy lineup in a physics arena.

Keep the core decision intact: every purchase in a preparation costs ~×1.5 the previous one and the price drops back after each fight, so the player constantly chooses "buy and merge one more time" vs "fight now". Keep the verified rules in #build-rules (R01–R20): 15-cell board, merge two identical tiers into the next tier, stat ladder, coins per hit, gears from kills, gems on wins, lineup returns after every fight, defeat still pays, spawn-level casing, gem shop, boss every 6th level, Freeze unlocked by the first boss.

Target: portrait browser window, one thumb, playable from the first touch (level 1 starts with one spinner and FIGHT), understandable without sound. Session form: 20–40 s levels in an endless ladder of 6-level chapters, with save/continue.

Design what the sources leave open (see Design space): tiers 11–50, enemy and boss roster beyond level 14, the abilities unlocked at levels 19 and 31, economy curves, fight stalemate handling. Bosses and spinners must be ORIGINAL designs — never the third-party characters seen in the source. No ads, purchases, missions or daily rewards.

Design the first 20 minutes from the first-session plan so the game hooks like successful Roblox games; apply the bridge rows and the art direction. Aim for better art, clarity and feel than the source. Plan, build, play-test on a phone-sized viewport with touch, fix, and report design decisions and actual test coverage against the acceptance cases. A demo, a first chapter only, or a promise to finish later is not completion.

Scope, version and readiness

Source model: the 2025 build in V2 (levels 1–14, spinner tiers 1–10, spawn levels 1–4, two bosses). V1 (2022) is an earlier build used only where it agrees (grid size, coin popup values) or to show history. The current store build (iOS 11.6.0, redesign in 11.5.0, Aug 2026) was not observed. Audio: the downloaded clips contain sound but no audio-capable inspection was available, so all sound is an adaptation brief, not a source match. Readiness: the complete-game specification is ready with named limits (Unknown rows below); nothing blocks the build.

Core statements (testable)

  1. C1 — Buy or fight. The player decides how many more base spinners to buy under a price that grows ×1.5 per purchase; fighting resets the price, so the next preparation is cheap again.
  2. C2 — Merge trades total for concentration. Two tier-N spinners become one tier-N+1 with ~0.7–0.8 of their summed Heart/Sword, freeing a cell; the board's 15 cells make this trade necessary.
  3. C3 — Arrangement, then watch. The enemy lineup is visible before FIGHT; after FIGHT the only input is the Freeze ability (once unlocked). The outcome changes what the player buys and merges next.
  4. C4 — Failure is a timeout, not a reset. Defeat keeps the lineup, pays coins and gears, and the player retries the same level with a cheaper buy button.

Entities and values

E1 — Spinner tiers. Heart / Sword: L1 12/3 (orange), L2 20/5 (purple), L3 28/7 (cyan), L4 44/11 (blue), L5 64/16 (red), L6 92/23 (gold), L7 140/35 (indigo shuriken), L8 208/52 (orange-white), L9 308/77 (red), L10 464/116 (dark grey and red). Tiers 11–50 exist in the collection count (50) but were not seen: design space.

E2 — Enemies. Enemy spinners use the same tiers. Counts seen: L1 1, L2 2, L3 2, L4–5 3, L7 3, L8 4, L13 3. Boss L6: one large humanoid (stands, long HP bar). Boss L12: two humanoids. Later bosses: unknown.

E3 — Rewards seen. Normal win gems: 2 (levels 1–5), 3 (levels 7–11), 4 (levels 13–14). Gears per result: 15 → ~300. Coins per result: 90K → ~2.4M; balances reach ~25M by level 13.

E4 — Abilities. Freeze (unlock: first boss). Slot 2: "Reach Lvl 19". Slot 3: "Reach Lvl 31". Contents of slots 2–3: unknown.

E5 — Side systems (omitted). Missions (3 tasks, coin rewards, ad skips), Daily Bonus (7 days, legendary spinner), ad multiplier wheel (×2–×5), ad FREE spinner, iOS purchases.

Principles (interpretation, guidance for design)

  • Situations come from lineups, not new rules: each level is a new enemy row against the same board.
  • Teaching is by interruption: each new system arrives as one full-screen card or one pointing hand at the moment it first matters (unlock card, build casing, Freeze hand).
  • Escalation is tier inflation on both sides plus a boss every six levels; the player's answer is merging and the spawn level.
  • Reward is paid on every fight, including losses, so no session ends empty-handed; the bigger rewards (gems, boss bonus, a new tier card) mark progress.

Art direction and signals

Style thesis: a glossy toy-box arena — chunky spinning tops with bold silhouettes, a white tray with a thick cyan rim on a warm yellow surround, magenta for commitment (FIGHT), green for buying, gold for coins, pink for gems, red for bosses. Keep the readable grammar of the source, raise the finish: cleaner materials, stronger spin motion blur, clearer HP bars and tier badges. Camera: fixed top-down-tilted view of the whole tray; enemies in the upper half, the 5×3 board in the lower half, HUD (level, chapter bar, coins, gems) at the top, buy/FIGHT/ability buttons below the tray so the thumb never covers the board. Coin popups and particles must not hide HP bars at the moment of a hit.

Assets. Spinners, bosses and arena: original 3D-rendered or stylised 2D sprites in one family (same lighting angle, outline weight and palette), ideally licensed ready assets (CC0 / permissive) or generated work processed for consistency; never the source's art or third-party characters. UI and fonts: a chunky rounded display face under an OFL licence, subsetted and inlined. Effects: code-driven particles. Record every third-party file (page, author, licence) and show credits inside the game.

Audio brief (not heard in the source). Events: buy (short coin clink), merge (electric zap + rising chime, louder for a first-time tier), fight launch (whoosh + spin-up hum), contact (metallic clink; pitch rises with tier), kill (puff + confetti pop), gear collect (soft tick), victory (short brass-like sting), defeat (soft descending tone), Freeze (icy crack), boss intro (low drum hit). Music: upbeat light electronic/pop loop for preparation, a slightly faster variation for fights, a heavier variation for boss levels; quiet under SFX. Start audio after the first touch; everything must read without sound.
